data.name: Namibia
data.summary: Namibia taxes only income from a Namibian source, residence being largely irrelevant. There is no capital gains tax (except on mining and petroleum rights and shares in companies holding them), dividends are exempt for resident individuals, and there is no wealth, inheritance, estate or gift tax. Foreign dividends and gains on a foreign portfolio are therefore untaxed. Property purchases bear transfer and stamp duty.

regimes.name: Namibian resident (source-based)
regimes.description: Source-based income tax 0-37% (2025/26 table); no CGT; dividends exempt; no inheritance or wealth tax.
regimes.eligibility: Tax applies to Namibian-source income regardless of residence; immigration requires a residence or work permit.

capital_gains.summary: No capital gains tax. Only profits on the sale of mining or petroleum licences/rights and on shares (direct or indirect) in companies owning such rights are taxable as specific inclusions in gross income. Receipts of a capital nature are excluded from gross income, and foreign-source amounts are outside the tax.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Transfer duty on shares in property- or mining-right-owning entities from 1 October 2024 (buyer-side).

capital_gains.rate_basis: No CGT: listed and foreign shares, private business sales (other than mineral/petroleum-right companies) and real estate held as capital 0%.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Profits from a scheme of profit-making (e.g. regular dealing in property or shares) are revenue, not capital, and taxed at up to 37% if Namibian-source.

dividends.summary: Dividends are exempt from tax for resident individuals. Foreign dividends are not Namibian-source and are also exempt; PwC notes that, because of the source rules and the exempt status of dividends, few foreign-taxed items are taxable in Namibia.
dividends.important_exceptions: Interest arising outside Namibia can be deemed Namibian-source for a resident (PwC); this concerns interest, not dividends.

dividends.rate_basis: 0% domestic (exempt) and 0% foreign (not Namibian-source / dividend exemption). Foreign withholding tax is a final cost; no credit needed.
dividends.withholding_outbound: Non-resident shareholders tax: 10% where a company holds at least 25%, otherwise 20%; treaty relief available.
dividends.treaty_network: 11 DTAs (Botswana, France, Germany, India, Malaysia, Mauritius, Romania, Russia, South Africa, Sweden, UK); none with the US.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 30% (financial years from 1 January 2025) on Namibian-source income; dividends exempt.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth or worth tax.

sources.title: Namibia, Republic of - Individual - Other taxes

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal property rates on municipal valuations. Transfer duty on property purchases by individuals on a sliding scale (12% for non-natural persons), with a luxury bracket above NAD 12 million from 1 October 2024; stamp duty NAD 12 per NAD 1,000 on transfer deeds.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax (PwC). Transfer of Namibian immovable property to heirs may attract transfer and stamp duty; this was not verified.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Transfer duty/stamp duty on registering inherited Namibian property not verified.

sources.title: Namibia, Republic of - Individual - Other taxes

residency.tax_residency_test: Not normally relevant: Namibia taxes income from Namibian sources (or deemed Namibian sources) regardless of residence; some foreign interest and royalties of 'ordinarily resident' persons are deemed Namibian-source (PwC).

routes.name: Permanent or temporary residence permit
routes.requirements: Non-citizens need a residence permit (or work permit); no residence-by-investment programme verified in this session.

corporate.summary: Source-based CIT of 30% for domestic companies and branches (financial years from 1 January 2025); special rates for registered manufacturers (first ten years), mining, diamond mining and petroleum. Dividend NRST 10%/20% on payments to non-residents.

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain fully US-taxed on worldwide income and estates; the app adds the US federal layer. No US-Namibia income tax treaty; Namibia's source basis means little local tax overlaps with US tax.
open_questions: Any announced move from source to residence-based taxation, or a capital gains tax, could not be checked in this session (web search budget exhausted); PwC (reviewed 16 July 2026) still describes a source system without CGT.
The 2026/27 individual tax table was not opened directly (PwC shows the 2025/26 table with a 37% top rate).

succession.name: Namibia
succession.summary: There is no forced heirship: freedom of testation is the first principle of Namibian wills law and is tied to Article 16 of the Constitution. Customary law governs many Black Namibians' estates. A 2018 review aims to unify succession law. Trusts and foundations were not sourced.
succession.family_claims: Not sourced. Succession law reform is under way (2018 ministerial statement).
succession.trust_note: Trusts: not sourced; 'yes' assumes Roman-Dutch trusts; unverified. No private-foundation law found.
open_questions: Maintenance claim of surviving spouse/dependants not sourced.
Trust law and foundations not sourced.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
Domestic trusts: likely available under the inherited common-law or Roman-Dutch tradition, but no statute or official source was read; confirm before marking yes.
